rules: Map the target READ-ONLY before hunting; never propose edits in this phase.
Identify languages/framework versions, dependency manifests, entry points, external inputs, and trust boundaries.
Locate where secrets, persistence, and network I/O live, and rank the highest-risk surfaces.
Emit NO findings here — this phase only produces the shared map later phases build on.
required_output: Entry points and external inputs (routes/handlers/CLI/URL schemes).
Trust boundaries and where secrets/persistence live.
Ranked list of highest-risk areas to investigate.
acceptance_checks: A later phase can find each risky surface from this map alone.
No finding-json blocks were emitted yet.
Dependency manifests and versions are enumerated, not guessed.

rules: Hunt real vulnerabilities: injection, broken authn/authz, insecure storage, weak TLS, over-broad permissions, vulnerable deps, PII leaks.
Cite file:line for every claim; a finding without a location is a guess.
Give a concrete exploit scenario and a safe, minimal fix per finding.
Emit each finding as a finding-json block with severity, category, confidence, file, title, fix.
required_output: Exploit scenario and concrete fix per finding.
acceptance_checks: Every finding is reproducible from its file:line + scenario.
No finding restates a guess as fact.
Severity reflects real exploitability, not theoretical risk.

rules: Find correctness/reliability bugs: races, swallowed errors, unhandled edges (nil/empty/off-by-one/overflow/timezone), lifecycle/leak issues, logic errors.
State the input or state that triggers the wrong behavior.
Cite file:line and give a minimal fix.
Emit each as a finding-json block.
acceptance_checks: Each bug has a concrete trigger, not just a code smell.
Fixes are minimal and don't drop features.

rules: Identify outdated/abandoned deps, deprecated APIs, worthwhile modern-idiom refactors, dead code, and performance issues.
Give current-vs-recommended and the migration effort/risk.
Do not propose churn for its own sake — tie each item to a concrete benefit.
Emit each as a finding-json block.
acceptance_checks: Each recommendation names a concrete benefit.
Breaking-change risk is called out where it exists.

rules: Synthesize ALL prior findings into ONE prioritized, de-duplicated report; do NOT vote findings away.
Group Critical/High/Medium/Low and open with a 3-line severity-count summary.
End with the top 5 fixes to do first.
The ranked list itself is assembled deterministically by the tool — keep prose honest and non-duplicative.
acceptance_checks: No finding from an earlier phase was dropped.
A reader knows the top 5 things to fix first.
